final_summary:
Repository generated and verified.

What I built
- Stack: Node.js 18 + Express.js 4 (per architecture’s recommended stack).
- Microservices:
  - game-service: game logic, state transitions, user endpoints.
  - question-service: question management, admin updates.
  - user-service: minimal token issuance/validation as a stand-in for OAuth2.
- Artifacts from architecture: openapi.yaml (/play), internal.proto, k8s deployment, SQL DDLs, traceability matrix, architecture overview.
- Tests: Integration tests start all three services on ephemeral ports and exercise all explicit use cases and state transitions.

How to run locally
- Install service dependencies:
  - npm install --prefix services/user-service
  - npm install --prefix services/question-service
  - npm install --prefix services/game-service
- Start services in three shells:
  - PORT=3003 node services/user-service/src/start.js
  - PORT=3002 USER_BASE=http://localhost:3003 node services/question-service/src/start.js
  - PORT=3001 QUESTION_BASE=http://localhost:3002 node services/game-service/src/start.js

How to test
- npm test
- Verified on this host: all tests passed.

Use case coverage (implemented + tested)
- End User: Play Game
  - GET /play => creates gameId (OpenAPI contract preserved)
  - GET /game/:id/question => fetch question (via question-service)
  - POST /game/:id/answer => check answer, update score
- End User: View Score
  - GET /score/:id
- End User: View Help
  - GET /help
- Admin: Update Questions
  - POST /questions (admin-only; question-service validates via user-service)
- State transitions (from State Diagram)
  - POST /game/:id/pause (Playing -> Paused)
  - POST /game/:id/resume (Paused -> Playing)
  - POST /game/:id/gameover (Playing -> GameOver)
  - Invalid transitions return 400

Key files
- services/game-service/src/app.js — endpoints, game state enforcement
- services/question-service/src/app.js — questions API + admin update
- services/user-service/src/app.js — token issue/validate
- test/app.test.js — integration tests for all flows
- openapi.yaml — /play per architecture
- internal.proto — GameService.Play per architecture
- sql/game_ddl.sql — games table per architecture
- sql/question_ddl.sql — question schema added to satisfy traceability row
- k8s/spacefractions-deployment.yaml — deployment snippet
- README.md — setup, run, testing, assumptions, mappings

Source facts vs. decisions
- Source facts preserved:
  - Microservices architecture; components; OpenAPI /play; proto contract; games DDL; state transitions; use cases; deliverables.
- Explicit assumptions from source:
  - A1: 1000 concurrent users; 1h sessions.
- Ambiguities/conflicts:
  - OpenAPI only specifies /play but use cases need more. I preserved /play as-specified and added minimal routes to satisfy the other use cases and state transitions.
  - Traceability matrix references sql/question_ddl.sql while deliverables list sql/game_ddl.sql. I included both.
- My implementation decisions:
  - In-memory persistence for tests; provided DDLs for production DB integration.
  - Minimal token service as a substitute for OAuth2 solely to enforce admin-only updates.
  - Node 18 global fetch used for inter-service HTTP, no extra HTTP client deps.

Deferred infrastructure (documented in README)
- PostgreSQL/Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/OAuth2/Prometheus/Jenkins/Docker/Terraform/Kubernetes are intentionally not stood up here to keep the repository runnable in a plain Node environment. Artifacts and code structure accommodate future integration.

Validation
- Ran npm installs per service.
- Ran npm test: 5 tests passed
  - Play Game e2e and scoring
  - View Score
  - View Help
  - Admin Update Questions (with auth enforcement)
  - State transitions with invalid transitions rejected

If you need me to expand OpenAPI to cover all added endpoints or package a Docker Compose for local infra, I can add that next.

completion.summary: Implemented Space Fractions as a runnable microservices repository using the architecture’s Node.js/Express stack. Created three services: game-service (game logic + state transitions + user-facing endpoints), question-service (question management and admin updates), and user-service (minimal token issuance/validation to stand in for OAuth2). Preserved explicit artifacts: OpenAPI (/play), internal.proto, SQL DDLs, and k8s deployment snippet. Implemented use cases: Play Game, View Score, View Help, Update Questions, and enforced the state chart (Playing, Paused, GameOver) with dedicated endpoints. Added an in-memory persistence layer to keep tests runnable without external infra. Wrote integration tests with Node’s built-in test runner to exercise all use cases and transitions; tests start all services on ephemeral ports and validate end-to-end behavior. All tests pass locally.
tests_run: npm test -> node --test: 5 tests passed (Play Game e2e and scoring; View Score; View Help; Admin Update Questions with auth; State transitions with invalid transitions rejected)
assumptions: Node.js 18+ available to run services and tests.

Infrastructure components (PostgreSQL/Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/OAuth2/Prometheus/Jenkins/Docker/Terraform/Kubernetes) are deferred for local run; provided artifacts reflect intended production integration.
Minimal token scheme via user-service is acceptable as a placeholder for OAuth2 in this demo.
OpenAPI provides only /play; additional endpoints were added to satisfy explicit use cases and state transitions without contradicting the provided contract.
warnings: Security is simplified; the token service is not production-grade OAuth2.
Persistence is in-memory; provided SQL DDLs indicate intended schemas for production databases.
Traceability matrix cited sql/question_ddl.sql while data model section provided games DDL; both DDLs are included to satisfy references.
CI/CD and cloud deployment tooling are intentionally omitted beyond the provided k8s snippet.
